arabic_blocks: [900] حدثنا أبو اليمان قال: أخبرنا شعيب عن الزهري قال: سألته هل صلى النبي ﷺ يعني صلاة الخوف قال: أخبرني سالم أن عبد الله بن عمر رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال غزوت مع رسول الله ﷺ قبل نجد فوازينا العدو فصاففنا لهم فقام رسول الله ﷺ يصلي لنا فقامت طائفة معه تصلي وأقبلت طائفة على العدو وركع رسول الله ﷺ بمن معه وسجد سجدتين ثم انصرفوا مكان الطائفة التي لم تصل فجاؤوا فركع رسول الله ﷺ بهم ركعة وسجد سجدتين ثم سلم فقام كل واحد منهم فركع لنفسه ركعة وسجد سجدتين
english_blocks: Abu al-Yaman related to us. He said: Shu‘ayb informed us, from al-Zuhri.

He said: I asked him, ‘Did the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, pray?’—meaning the fear prayer. He said: Salim informed me that ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Umar, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both, said:

I went on an expedition with the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, towards Najd. We faced the enemy and formed ranks opposite them. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood to lead us in prayer. One group stood with him, praying, while another group faced the enemy. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, bowed with those who were with him and made two prostrations. Then they went to take the place of the group that had not prayed. That group came, and the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed one unit with them and made two prostrations. Then he gave the closing greeting. Each of them then stood and prayed one unit for himself and made two prostrations.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Shu‘ayb’s question to al-Zuhri and al-Zuhri’s report from Salim remain in the reading body, including informed me; the initial chain remains expandable. The prayer identification is the source’s own يعني clause, not an app explanation.
All selected honorifics, both group changes, the two-prostration clauses, the closing greeting and each individual’s completion remain. No additional prayer mechanics are supplied.

The modern print matches the selected Messenger designation and explicit تصلي after the first group stands. Brill has النبي at the expedition opening and lacks that explicit تصلي; the selected digital wording remains unchanged.
Modern printed reference 942; individually matched English bodies Bewley 900 and pinned EPUB 2.14.64. The Quran quotation before this report is separate chapter context, not narration.

arabic_blocks: [901] حدثنا سعيد بن يحيى بن سعيد القرشي قال: حدثني أبي قال: حدثنا ابن جريج عن موسى بن عقبة عن نافع عن ابن عمر نحوا من قول مجاهد إذا اختلطوا قياما وزاد بن عمر عن النبي ﷺ وإن كانوا أكثر من ذلك فليصلوا قياما وركبانا
english_blocks: Sa‘id ibn Yahya ibn Sa‘id al-Qurashi related to us. He said: My father related to me. He said: Ibn Jurayj related to us, from Musa ibn ‘Uqbah, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar:

Something similar to Mujahid’s statement: When they become intermingled, they pray standing. Ibn ‘Umar added, from the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace: ‘If they are more numerous than that, let them pray standing or mounted.’
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: This is the selected source’s abbreviated attribution to a statement of Mujahid followed by Ibn ‘Umar’s addition from the Prophet. No report number, missing earlier wording, head gesture or additional narrator route has been inserted.

The words they pray make explicit the grammatical ellipsis before قياما. Al-‘Ayni expressly identifies the omitted construction as يصلون قياما. This narrowly stated translation choice is documented separately; no legal conclusion from the commentary is added.

The selected pronouns and comparative أكثر من ذلك are retained. The English comparisons identify the enemy and expand the battle setting; those explanatory nouns and the EPUB’s individually are not inserted into the working text.

Both prints support the full chain, first-person my father related to me, abbreviated Mujahid comparison and final addition. Modern printed reference 943; English bodies Bewley 901 and pinned EPUB 2.14.65. The heading’s راجل قائم gloss is retained in the provisional heading, separate from this numbered report.

arabic_blocks: [902] حدثنا حيوة بن شريح قال: حدثنا محمد بن حرب عن الزبيدي عن الزهري عن عبيد الله بن عبد الله بن عتبة عن ابن عباس رضى الله تعالى عنهما قال قام النبي ﷺ وقام الناس معه فكبر وكبروا معه وركع وركع ناس منهم ثم سجد وسجدوا معه ثم قام للثانية فقام الذين سجدوا وحرسوا إخوانهم وأتت الطائفة الأخرى فركعوا وسجدوا معه والناس كلهم في صلاة ولكن يحرس بعضهم بعضا
english_blocks: Haywah ibn Shurayh related to us. He said: Muhammad ibn Harb related to us, from al-Zubaydi, from al-Zuhri, from ‘Ubaydullah ibn ‘Abdullah ibn ‘Utbah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, may Allah Most High be pleased with them both. He said:

The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, stood, and the people stood with him. He said ‘Allah is greatest,’ and they said it with him. He bowed, and some of the people bowed. Then he prostrated, and they prostrated with him. Then he stood for the second unit. Those who had prostrated stood and guarded their brothers. The other group came and bowed and prostrated with him. All the people were in prayer, but they were guarding one another.

notes: The full Haywah–Muhammad–al-Zubaydi–al-Zuhri–‘Ubaydullah–Ibn ‘Abbas chain remains, with the source honorific. No additional chain or prayer instruction is supplied.

The distinction between everyone standing, some bowing, the second unit, those guarding, and the other group is retained. The closing present-state phrase says all were in prayer, not merely that everyone eventually completed prayer.
Both prints support the complete sequence. Modern printed reference 944; individually matched English bodies Bewley 902 and pinned EPUB 2.14.66.

arabic_blocks: [903] حدثنا يحيى قال: حدثنا وكيع عن علي بن مبارك عن يحيى بن أبي كثير عن أبي سلمة عن جابر بن عبد الله قال جاء عمر يوم الخندق فجعل يسب كفار قريش ويقول يا رسول الله ما صليت العصر حتى كادت الشمس أن تغيب، فقال النبي ﷺ وأنا والله ما صليتها بعد قال: فنزل إلى بطحان فتوضأ وصلى العصر بعد ما غابت الشمس ثم صلى المغرب بعدها
english_blocks: Yahya related to us. He said: Waki‘ related to us, from ‘Ali ibn Mubarak, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abdullah. He said:

‘Umar came on the day of the Ditch and began cursing the unbelievers of Quraysh, saying, ‘Messenger of Allah, I had not prayed ‘Asr until the sun was almost setting.’ The Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, said, ‘And by Allah, I have not prayed it yet either.’ He said: He went down to Buthan, performed ablution and prayed ‘Asr after the sun had set. Then he prayed Maghrib after it.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: The selected chain names the first transmitter only Yahya, as does the modern print. Brill supplies Yahya ibn Ja‘far al-Bukhari. That longer identity is noted here, not inserted into the selected chain.

‘Umar’s first time statement has كادت, almost setting; the later actual prayer occurs after sunset. Both prints and Bewley preserve this distinction. The pinned EPUB’s first speech says the sun has set; that temporal difference is not adopted.

The oath, still-not-prayed statement, descent to Buthan, ablution and ordered ‘Asr then Maghrib remain. Modern printed reference 945; English bodies Bewley 903 and pinned EPUB 2.14.67. The earlier al-Awza‘i, Makhul and Anas chapter material remains separate Arabic context.

arabic_blocks: [904] حدثنا عبد الله بن محمد بن أسماء قال: حدثنا جويرية عن نافع عن ابن عمر قال: قال النبي ﷺ لنا لما رجع من الأحزاب لا يصلين أحد العصر إلا في بني قريظة فأدرك بعضهم العصر في الطريق، فقال بعضهم لا نصلي حتى نأتيها، وقال بعضهم بل نصلي لم يرد منا ذلك فذكر للنبي ﷺ فلم يعنف واحدا منهم
english_blocks: ‘Abdullah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma’ related to us. He said: Juwayriyah related to us, from Nafi‘, from Ibn ‘Umar. He said:

When the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, returned from al-Ahzab, he said to us, ‘Let no one pray ‘Asr except at Banu Qurayzah.’ The time for ‘Asr reached some of them on the way. Some said, ‘We will not pray until we reach it.’ Others said, ‘Rather, we will pray; that was not intended of us.’ This was mentioned to the Prophet, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, and he did not rebuke any of them.

arabic_blocks: [905] حدثنا مسدد قال: حدثنا حماد عن عبد العزيز بن صهيب وثابت البناني عن أنس بن مالك أن رسول الله ﷺ صلى الصبح بغلس ثم ركب، فقال الله أكبر خربت خيبر إنا إذا نزلنا بساحة قوم { فساء صباح المنذرين } فخرجوا يسعون في السكك ويقولون محمد والخميس قال والخميس الجيش فظهر عليهم رسول الله ﷺ فقتل المقاتلة وسبي الذراري فصارت صفية لدحية الكلبي وصارت لرسول الله ﷺ ثم تزوجها وجعل صداقها عتقها، فقال عبد العزيز لثابت يا أبا محمد أنت سألت أنسا ما أمهرها قال أمهرها نفسها فتبسم
english_blocks: Musaddad related to us. He said: Hammad related to us, from ‘Abd al-‘Aziz ibn Suhayb and Thabit al-Bunani, from Anas ibn Malik:

The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, prayed the dawn prayer while it was still dark. Then he mounted and said, ‘Allah is greatest! Khaybar is ruined. When we descend into a people’s open space, evil is the morning of those who have been warned.’ They came out running in the streets, saying, ‘Muhammad and al-khamis!’ He said: Al-khamis means the army. The Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace, overcame them, killed the fighting men and took the children captive. Safiyyah came to Dihyah al-Kalbi, and then to the Messenger of Allah, may Allah bless him and grant him peace. He then married her and made her freedom her bridal gift.
‘Abd al-‘Aziz said to Thabit, ‘Abu Muhammad, did you ask Anas what he gave her as a bridal gift?’ He said, ‘He gave her herself as her bridal gift.’ Then he smiled.
entries.english_status: Personal prototype: AI-assisted working translation; two Arabic printed witnesses and two English translation families compared. Independent Arabic, English and context review pending.

notes: Both narrators from Anas are retained. Brill names Hammad ibn Zayd and Anas ibn Malik in the final question; the selected digital text and modern print use Hammad and Anas at those positions. No longer name has been silently supplied.

The source’s al-khamis word and its own army gloss remain in the report, as do the fighting men, children taken captive, sequence involving Dihyah and the Messenger, marriage and manumission as the bridal gift. The working English uses children for الذراري, as Bewley does; the Khan-family body expands this to children and women. That expansion is not silently adopted.
The Quran-linked expression retains only the source’s quoted wording. No additional verse text, troop count, motive, judgement or ruling is inserted.

The final ‘Abd al-‘Aziz–Thabit question, answer and smile are present in both Arabic prints and Bewley. They are absent from pinned EPUB 2.14.68, along with the army gloss; the complete selected ending remains in the reading text and script.
